reviewer_role: independent read-only source, assumption-boundary and evidence reviewer

protected_input_verification.only_prior_source_change: TheoryCompletion.lean contains exactly the three new import lines; removing those lines yields the exact baseline blob.

evidence_verification.method: Read actual Git blobs and assert their SHA256/byte lengths against pinned manifests; inspect statements and logs; do not infer pass from labels alone.
evidence_verification.test_evidence_assessment: RELEASE_ACCEPTANCE explicitly describes author-observed command exits and summaries and does not assert newly archived raw test logs; reviewer did not repeat these tests.
evidence_verification.results_and_boundaries_assessment: Matches reviewed mathematics and preserves finite-horizon positivity, state-only projection, numerical homogeneity, no infinite conditioned-process implication, no executable-controller synthesis and no scientific-closure promotion.

typed_semantic_reuse_review.method: Read the complete current source declarations, hypotheses, definitions and proof call paths of each candidate pair; distinguish actual direct or transitive reuse from different event or source interfaces. No new native pairwise run was performed.

pairs.hypothesis_and_semantic_comparison: The existing theorem requires a fixed surjective encoder C and a chosen representative and identifies the representative macro-model row with the encoded micro row. The new row maps z to (z, update m a (q z)), depending on the current memory and recorded action. It has no fixed surjective quotient or representative premise. Applying the existing theorem would require a new artificial quotient interface and would not itself establish the actual memory-update row.
pairs.actual_reuse: The new proof directly uses Model.transitionPMF_apply_toReal, PMF.ext, and finite PMF toReal equality. It is a short row-adapter, not an independence or novelty claim.

pairs.hypothesis_and_semantic_comparison: The existing theorem assumes an equivalence e of one target state space and e composed with q equals r, and transports an already constructed pushforward row under relabeling. The action- and memory-dependent graph map z to (z, update m a (q z)) is not supplied as such a whole-space equivalence; the new theorem establishes the original numerical row of a newly constructed augmented Model. The relabeling hypotheses and conclusion do not replace this obligation.
pairs.actual_reuse: Ordinary PMF mapping and extensional equality are reused without adding unused relabeling hypotheses.

pairs.hypothesis_and_semantic_comparison: The existing theorem computes total survival for a stationary current-observation policy on a fixed finite Model. The new theorem concerns the original experiment driven by an autonomous finite-memory controller. The constructed augmented Model, observation Prod.snd and action law controller.action meet the existing stationary interface.
pairs.actual_reuse: actual_finite_survival_eq_killed_mass -> projected_survival_mass -> SameSourceSafePrefixCheck.homogeneous_survival_real_eq_killed_pow_sum -> SameSourceKilledPathCheck.actual_survival_mass_eq_killed_pow_sum. FiniteMemoryPhysicalSafety.actual_state_prefix_event_mass and actual_safe_prefix_pullback establish equality with the original finite-memory experiment.

pairs.hypothesis_and_semantic_comparison: The existing theorem is a single-terminal joint survival mass for the stationary observation-policy experiment. The new theorem requires the total survival mass of the actual finite-memory experiment. One could apply the terminal theorem on augmented states and sum, but the already available total-mass bridge supplies precisely that required result.
pairs.actual_reuse: The new proof uses the existing total-mass theorem through the bridge above. The old terminal and total theorems both reach state_terminal_mass_eq_killed_pow. No direct dependency on actual_survival_terminal_mass_eq_killed_pow is invented, and no independent result is claimed.

pairs.hypothesis_and_semantic_comparison: The existing theorem converts a nonnegative finite row of sum one to its exact PMF values. The new positive remaining-survival hypothesis selects the positive totalWindowRow branch; finiteWindowRowPMF has already supplied the nonnegativity and normalization proofs required by the existing theorem.

The existing theorem assumes a measurable Markov kernel and causal policy and proves unconditional consistency of an infinite complete-history measure with its recursively composed finite law. The new theorem assumes finite nonnegative Q, nonnegative eta, positive Z_T and n<=T and computes every conditioned prefix atom as a killed product times its remaining-survival weight divided by Z_T. General prefix consistency supplies neither the initial tilt nor the suffix-weight identity nor the zero-row cancellation needed for this formula.
pairs.actual_reuse: The new proof uses causalLaw/pmfExtend recursion, finiteWindowRow normalization, and nonnegative remaining-survival recursion. The existing infinite-history consistency theorem cannot substitute for the new atom computation. This is an interface assessment, not a logical independence claim.

pairs.hypothesis_and_semantic_comparison: The existing theorem identifies an unconditioned original finite-memory experiment after state projection with the finite prefix of its projected infinite state trajectory, allowing numerical rows to depend on time. The new theorem compares independently generated tilted time-dependent rows with a positive-survival-conditioned state prefix of the stationary original experiment. The unconditional projection identity does not prove the conditioning, tilt or changed row law.
pairs.actual_reuse: The new proof uses actual_conditioned_prefix_mass and state_safe_atom_eq_matrixPathWeight. actual_conditioned_prefix_mass -> actual_prefix_survival_mass -> actual_state_path_eq_stationary_path supplies the same-source foundation. No direct dependency on this unrelated finite-memory prefix endpoint is invented.

pairs.hypothesis_and_semantic_comparison: The existing theorem replays actual recorded actions into initialized and updated memory and identifies the unconditioned state-memory prefix with the corresponding infinite augmented trajectory. The new theorem has no memory replay target: it identifies the survival-conditioned state prefix with independently generated finite-window rows. Augmentation alone does not establish the terminal survival tilt or the conditioned prefix weights.
pairs.actual_reuse: The new proof reuses the existing actual conditioned-prefix mass calculation and same-source path bridge; it does not claim the unconditional augmentation theorem proves the conditioned identity.

pairs.hypothesis_and_semantic_comparison: The existing theorem relates the unconditioned stationary original action/state experiment, after action erasure, to a homogeneous infinite trajectory prefix. The new theorem assumes positive survival through T and identifies a horizon-dependent tilted initial PMF and totalized nonhomogeneous rows with the filtered experiment. The existing unconditional homogeneous prefix theorem does not supply these changes of law.
pairs.actual_reuse: Both interfaces rest on actual_state_path_eq_stationary_path. The new theorem reaches it through actual_conditioned_prefix_mass and actual_prefix_survival_mass, and additionally proves all-atom finite-window weights including zero rows.

retained_mathematical_limits: The finite-window interpretation requires Z_T>0 and n<=T, including T=0.
The actual conditioned identity retains complete state prefixes, not reconstructed full action histories.
Homogeneous memory survival requires a fixed numerical source; support homogeneity alone is insufficient.
The state-memory chain need not make its state-only projection Markov.
No cross-horizon conditioned infinite process, positive infinite survival, QSD assumption or executable controller synthesis is supplied.
